title: No test proves another gym is refused on busy machines, Bring a friend counts, the leaderboard owner view, the challenge reward confirm, or the entry machine screens
what: Each of these owner calls works out the gym from the sign-in key and only touches that gym's rows, so reading the code found no leak. But the database tests never try them with a second gym's key. The busy machines test makes a second gym's owner key and never uses it; the Bring a friend counts are only asked by the gym's own owner; the leaderboard owner view and the challenge reward confirm are only tested on each gym's own records. The five entry machine owner calls (add or remove a machine, give a member a machine number, send machine orders, the list) are live on the server and have no test of their own at all, only the line saying they may be called without signing in. A later change that drops the gym check would still pass the build.
expected: For every owner call this area uses, a database test tries it with another gym's owner key and proves it sees, changes and removes nothing of the first gym.
how_often: no harm today; only if a later change breaks the gym check
fix_line: Add a second-gym check to the busy machines, Bring a friend, leaderboard and reward tests, and write a test file for the entry machine owner calls before that feature goes live

items.reason: These screens reach the gym server only through database calls that each take the device's sign-in key: owner_member_measurements, owner_save_measurement, owner_delete_measurement, owner_diet_plans, owner_save_diet_plan, owner_withdraw_diet_plan (any staff of the key's gym); owner_challenges, owner_board (any staff); owner_save_challenge, owner_cancel_challenge, owner_hide_on_board, owner_confirm_challenge_reward (owner only); owner_gym_timings (any staff), owner_save_gym_timings (owner only); owner_machine_setup (any staff), owner_save_machine_setup (owner only); owner_friend_summary (any staff); owner_entry_machines, owner_set_machine_numbers, owner_queue_machine_commands (any staff), owner_add_entry_machine, owner_remove_entry_machine (owner only); owner_member_photos, owner_save_member_photo, owner_remove_member_photo (any staff). All are callable by anon and signed-in users (the key is the gate) and all scope to the key's gym. Members, visits, enquiries, expenses, payments and imports go through crm_push, where the server refuses expense, plan and gym edits and payment changes from a desk key (0019), matching the screens' hidden buttons. The import AI goes through the panel Worker, which allows the owner only. Registering an entry machine trusts the serial alone and the first gym to type it wins (an owner could claim another gym's not-yet-registered machine; DUPLICATE_SERIAL also tells anyone a serial is taken): same root cause as the existing serial-only finding, so its id is reused.

No per-gym row rules here: every table this area reaches (gym_body_measurements, gym_diet_plans, gym_challenges, gym_challenge_hits, gym_board_meta, gym_member_board, gym_timings, gym_machine_setup, gym_machine_guesses, gym_friend_invites, gym_friend_referrals, gym_member_photos, entry_machines, entry_machine_members, entry_machine_commands, crm_records) has row security on and no policy, so apps cannot read or write them directly; security.sql check 5 proves anon and a signed-in user with no gym read nothing. Another gym refused, by test: measurements and diet plans 0035 (steps 5 and 12); gym timings 0036 (step 5); challenges list, save, cancel and hide 0037 (steps 6 and 8) and 0091 (step 3); member photos 0043 (step 7); crm_records security.sql 6a/6b. No second-gym test: gym_machine_setup (0049), the friend tables (0056), gym_challenge_hits through the reward confirm (0047/0048), the leaderboard owner view (0037), and every entry machine owner call (no test file for 0059).
Rule applied: the tables and calls with no second-gym test are one finding (busy machines, Bring a friend, reward confirm, leaderboard owner view, entry machines).
Rule applied: no live cross-gym attempt was run; only code and the existing tests were read, and no gym's rows were queried.
The key-pattern scan has no hit in these screens, and the screens hold no key: every call sends only the device's own sign-in key. Panel only, so no APK.

No AI key in the browser. The AI assistant page only shows the assistant module; the import's column guess goes to the panel Worker with the sign-in key, and the Worker holds the AI key, allows the owner only and keeps a daily limit per gym.
These screens hold no sign-in, PIN, PIN reset or session code (that lives in the auth area). The entry machine number on a member page is the id a finger or face is enrolled under, not a password.

No raw HTML anywhere in these screens (no dangerouslySetInnerHTML, innerHTML or eval), so typed text and the web page visitor's chat show as plain text. Call and WhatsApp links use digits only; the app-link share opens with noopener. Spreadsheet downloads (losing-the-habit list, skipped import rows) guard cells starting with = + - @. The database calls take parameters, build no SQL from text, and cap text lengths.

Two uploads. The member import file is read in the browser only, refused over 5 MB, and parsed by the fixed SheetJS 0.20.3. The member photo goes to the server as base64, which accepts only a JPEG of at most 100,000 bytes for a live member of the key's own gym.

The only shared link built here is the app link with the gym's join code (sent on purpose to the member); challenge winners are copied as text. No link here carries a member id or a secret; the /j/<code> and gym page links themselves belong to the web pages area.

npm audit's two SheetJS alerts point at node_modules/xlsx 0.18.5, which belongs to the phone app; the panel's import uses its own SheetJS 0.20.3 from SheetJS's site, past both fixes (0.19.3, 0.20.2). No other alert names a library these screens use. Outside this area: the phone app's xlsx 0.18.5 is still open to both.
